newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas off sharply as one big seller moves volu.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas off sharply as one big seller moves volu.

text.p: UK natural gas prices fell sharply in all periods in busy trade on Friday, traders and brokers said, with one major seller seen as behind most of the movement in the market.
A trader for the major seller said they had concluded around 20 trades, including several in the gas year from October 1997.
The lowest trade was heard done at 13.00 pence a therm, and the buyer said that this deal was done through a broker, indicating that the seller had realised less than 13 pence for the trade.
By the close, one broker said the gas year was bid at 12.90 pence a therm against offers at 13.10 pence. This compares with a bid/offer spread on Thursday of 13.30/13.50 pence a therm.

The third quarter saw even greater losses. Trade was done as low as 10.35 pence, with bids seen at 10.30 pence by the close. This is a loss of some 0.70 pence a therm from the bid price on Thursday night, with the months of July and August bid even lower - though not thought traded individually - by the close.
The only individual month heard done was June, which traded at 10.85 pence a therm, although again the bid/offer spread was well below this by the close.

The trader for the major seller said there was no particular reason for the heavy volume of sales at sharply lower prices, adding that it was "nothing different" from normal, and that in any case the last three trades had been purchases.

Another trader said that it was surprising the seller had not moved more discreetly to sell large volumes, saying: "I would think it may have been better to do it quietly. In this market, when you start hitting with volume, prices will move dramatically."

The IPE futures market reflected the lower physical market. A total of 180 lots were traded, all in the morning, with front month July dropping by 0.54 pence a therm to settle at 10.50 pence, although it was well below this by the close of business on the physical market.
